27 A stationary wave is formed on a stretched string. The diagram illustrates the string at an instant
of time when the displacement of the string is at its maximum.
string
fixed
point
fixed
point
P
The frequency of the wave is 250 Hz. Point P on the string has a vertical displacement of –1.0 mm.
What will be the vertical displacement of the point P after a time of 5.0 ms?
A
–1.0 mm
B
zero
C
+0.5 mm
D
+1.0 mm

hints: Notice the diagram shows the stationary wave at maximum displacement, with point P at the bottom of a loop at $-1.0\text{ mm}$.
Connect the given frequency of $250\text{ Hz}$ to the period $T = 1/f$ and compare the $5.0\text{ ms}$ delay with that period.
Recall each point on a stationary wave performs SHM, so track point P from a negative extreme for just over one full oscillation to find its next position.
walkthrough: Identify the vibration of point P: on a stationary wave every point performs SHM with frequency $250\text{ Hz}$, and P starts at its negative amplitude of $-1.0\text{ mm}$.
Calculate the period using $T = 1/f = 1/250\text{ Hz} = 0.0040\text{ s} = 4.0\text{ ms}$.
Express the waiting time as a number of periods: $5.0\text{ ms} / 4.0\text{ ms} = 1.25$, so the time is one full period plus one quarter period.
After one full period of $4.0\text{ ms}$ point P returns to $-1.0\text{ mm}$, then in the extra quarter period of $1.0\text{ ms}$ it moves from the extreme back toward equilibrium.
In SHM starting at an extreme, a quarter period later the displacement is zero, so after $1.25T$ the displacement of P is zero. This is option B.

A.explanation: This would be the displacement after a whole number of periods, but $5.0\text{ ms}$ is not a whole number of periods for $250\text{ Hz}$.

B.explanation: After $1.25$ periods point P has moved from its negative extreme through one full oscillation plus a quarter oscillation to the equilibrium position, so displacement is zero.

C.explanation: Point P performs SHM between $-1.0\text{ mm}$ and $+1.0\text{ mm}$, but at one and a quarter periods it is at zero, not at half amplitude.

D.explanation: This would be the opposite extreme after half a period, but $5.0\text{ ms}$ corresponds to $1.25$ periods, not $0.5$ periods.
